From aa8963fdce667a42fb7f0bdd2909fadcab02f9a8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Weiming Shi <bestswngs@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:33:13 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] tun: free page on build_skb failure in tun_xdp_one()

When build_skb() fails in tun_xdp_one(), the function sets ret to
-ENOMEM and jumps to the out label, which returns without freeing the
page that vhost_net_build_xdp() allocated for the frame. As with the
short-frame rejection path, tun_sendmsg() discards the per-buffer error
and still returns total_len, so vhost_tx_batch() takes the success path
and never frees the page. Each build_skb() failure in a batch leaks one
page-frag chunk.

Free the page before taking the error path, matching the put_page() the
other error exits of tun_xdp_one() already perform.

Fixes: 043d222f93ab ("tuntap: accept an array of XDP buffs through sendmsg()")
Reported-by: Xiang Mei <xmei5@asu.edu>
Signed-off-by: Weiming Shi <bestswngs@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Dongli Zhang <dongli.zhang@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Willem de Bruijn <willemb@google.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260521163312.1479805-2-bestswngs@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/tun.c b/drivers/net/tun.c
index f594360d66d6..9e7744eb57a3 100644
--- a/drivers/net/tun.c
+++ b/drivers/net/tun.c
@@ -2439,6 +2439,7 @@ static int tun_xdp_one(struct tun_struct *tun,
 build:
 	skb = build_skb(xdp->data_hard_start, buflen);
 	if (!skb) {
+		put_page(virt_to_head_page(xdp->data));
 		ret = -ENOMEM;
 		goto out;
 	}
-- 
2.34.1

**Summary of the patch**

This patch fixes a memory leak in the `tun_xdp_one()` function inside `drivers/net/tun.c`. When `build_skb()` fails, the function previously jumped to the error label without releasing the page that was allocated for the XDP frame. The added `put_page()` ensures the page is freed before returning.

**Modifications in each file**

- **`drivers/net/tun.c`**: In `tun_xdp_one()`, a single line is added: `put_page(virt_to_head_page(xdp->data));` before the `goto out;` on the `build_skb()` failure path. This releases the page fragment that was allocated for the XDP buffer.

**Relationships between the modifications**

There is only one file modified. The change is placed exactly where the memory leak occurs—inside the error handling branch for a failed `build_skb()`. The new code mirrors the existing `put_page()` calls already present in other error paths of the same function (e.g., when the frame length is too short), ensuring consistent resource cleanup. Without this fix, each `build_skb()` failure in a batch silently leaked a page, because the caller `tun_sendmsg()` discards per‑buffer errors and does not free the page.
